shared_elements: shallow relief / incised carving on the stone face
a distinct projecting upper element above a broader carved panel
curved or angled linear motifs arranged in repeated series
band-like elements running across the surface
ring or arc-shaped forms (weaker in A)
justification: Both are tall monolithic stones bearing low-relief carving organised as a narrower projecting upper element sitting above a wider decorated panel, with repeated linear motifs and band-like divisions, which is the closest correspondence. The differences dominate, however: A is a pale, fine-grained stone bearing crisp, angular herringbone/chevron rows in shallow incision, while B is a dark, coarse stone with rounded, plastic relief forms — rings, lobed shapes and curving bands — plus a modelled head, so the carving vocabulary and execution look unrelated.
